agent_notes: The superscription 'Song of the Ascents, of David' is verse 1 in the Hebrew numbering (KJV 131:0 plus 131:1); I translated it as part of the verse. I followed the Hebrew as given.

Rashi (Ps 131:1) links 'great things' to the buildings and plantings of his son; the packet quotes it but it is a midrashic reading, so I mention it only as a reading, not as the sense of the text. Ibn Ezra and Radak both take 'walked' as intransitive ('went about', not 'pursued'), which is why the literal layer reads 'walked in'.

agent_notes: Reviewer request addressed: the commentary no longer says Malbim and Ibn Ezra read the doubling as intensity. It now cites Ibn Ezra (the sense is doubled) and Metzudat David (the repetition expresses persistence), and states Malbim's own reading separately: the first verb goes with 'like a weaned child upon his mother' (trust in God alone), the second with 'like a weaned child upon me' (the soul silent like the child, knowing it has no strength of its own). The line 'the soul becomes the mother' is removed; the mother is God, as Malbim says.

Gloss corrected against STEPBible: pos 6 and 9 'gamul' is a passive participle ('weaned one'), not a verb; pos 1-2 'im lo' is glossed as the oath formula 'surely [if I have] not', following Radak, Meiri and Metzudat David. The Hebrew has no completed oath, so the literal layer keeps the bare 'if not' and the dramatic layer renders it as an assertion.

Judgment call on 'alai' (pos 10): the five English versions split (KJV 'even as', YLT 'by me', ASV 'within me', BBE drops it). I keep the literal 'upon me' in layer 1 and 'within me' in the dramatic layer, following Rashi ('in my inner part'), Metzudat David ('in my inside') and Ibn Ezra ('like in my eyes'). Unsourced: that the verb shiviti means 'I have levelled' is my reading of the root, supported by Ibn Ezra's gloss 'I have set'.
